method: 1. Build the skeleton first by memorising the Parts table and the Article ranges in the first seven formulas. Most 2021-2024 questions are one lookup away from this grid.
2. Attach three tags to every Article: what it does, who acts (President, Parliament, Governor, Rajya Sabha or Speaker), and the limit (1 month, 14 days, 6 months, 1/10, 2/3 or 15%).

3. Learn amendments as number-year-content triples and link each to the Article it created, for example 86th to 21A and 51A(k), 101st to 246A and 279A, and 104th to the end of Anglo-Indian nomination.

4. In statement questions, mark each statement true or false on its own. The usual swaps are Supreme Court and High Court, President and Governor, Parliament and Rajya Sabha, binding and advisory, exclusive and concurrent, and 1 month and 2 months.
5. In 'NOT a Fundamental Duty or Right' questions, strike out everything the text actually contains. Paying tax, voting, respecting elders and property as a Fundamental Right are the usual answers.
6. In chronology questions, write a year beside every item before you order them.

7. For current Polity (office holders, pending bills and new laws), refresh from PIB and PRS a month before the exam and prefer the officially accepted number, such as 25 High Courts, 245 Rajya Sabha members and 543 Lok Sabha seats.
traps: Art 72 is the President's pardon; the Governor's is Art 161 and it cannot pardon a death sentence.
Art 131 is the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction, not the High Courts'; water disputes are excluded (Art 262 lets Parliament bar the Supreme Court).
Inter-State Council is set up by the President under Art 263 and only advises; Zonal Councils are statutory (SR Act 1956) and chaired by the Home Minister.
GST Council recommendations are not binding; Art 246A is concurrent power (both Parliament and States), not exclusive to Parliament.
Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but not the other way; the Speaker, not the President, certifies it; the Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend it.
In a Concurrent-List conflict the Union law prevails, unless the State law was reserved and got the President's assent.
State Council of Ministers is responsible to the Legislative Assembly only, never to the Legislative Council.
Sixth Schedule: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; Nagaland and Arunachal are not included.
Art 50 (separation of judiciary) and Art 44 (UCC) are DPSPs, not Fundamental Rights; Art 51A is Duties.
Right to property is Art 300A (constitutional legal right), not a Fundamental Right since the 44th Amendment.
42nd added Fundamental Duties and 'socialist, secular, integrity'; 44th removed property and brought 'armed rebellion'; 86th added 21A and the 11th duty.
The Solicitor General is statutory; the Attorney General (Art 76) and Advocate General (Art 165) are constitutional.
National Emergency needs approval within 1 month; President's Rule and Financial Emergency within 2 months.
Art 131A (42nd) gave power to the Supreme Court, not High Courts, and was repealed by the 43rd.
Supreme Court strength: 'CJI + 33' was the answer until 2026; watch for the new total of 38 including the CJI.

examples.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India prohibits anyone from employing children below the age of fourteen in factories, mines, etc? 23 / 26 / 24 / 25 (CGL 2021)
examples.how: 1. The Right against Exploitation covers Arts 23 and 24. 2. Art 23 bans trafficking and forced labour, while Art 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines and hazardous work. 3. So the answer is Article 24.

examples.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India were borrowed from the ______ Constitution. Spanish / Norwegian / Irish / Australian (CGL 2021)
examples.how: 1. Ireland gave India the Directive Principles, nomination to the Rajya Sabha and the method of electing the President. 2. Australia gave the Concurrent List, so it is only a distractor. 3. The answer is Irish.

examples.q: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution of India ______. (CGL 2021)
examples.a: reduced the age for voting from 21 to 18 years
examples.how: 1. The 61st Amendment (1988, effective 1989) amended Art 326 and lowered the voting age from 21 to 18. 2. The 15% cap on ministers is the 91st Amendment, a different option.

examples.q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India pronounce the theory of the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution? Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973 / Golaknath Case, 1967 / Minerva Mills Case, 1980 / Swarn Singh Case (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. Golaknath (1967) held that Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights. 2. Kesavananda Bharati (1973), decided by 13 judges, allowed amendment of any part but not of the basic structure. 3. Minerva Mills (1980) applied the doctrine later, so the answer is Kesavananda Bharati.

examples.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in specific categories of matters? Article 144 / Article 145 / Article 142 / Article 143 (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. Art 143 is the Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction, under which the President seeks its opinion. 2. Art 142 is complete justice, Art 144 requires authorities to act in aid of the Court, and Art 145 covers rules of the Court.

examples.q: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction? Certiorari / Quo Warranto / Habeas Corpus / Prohibition (CGL 2024)
examples.how: 1. Prohibition stops a lower court that is exceeding its jurisdiction while the case is still pending. 2. Certiorari quashes an order that has already been passed. 3. The question describes a court going beyond its jurisdiction, so the key gives Prohibition.

examples.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution CANNOT be suspended even during an emergency declared on the grounds of war or external aggression? Articles 15 and 17 / Articles 20 and 21 / Articles 14 and 16 / Articles 30 and 32 (CGL 2024)
examples.how: 1. The 44th Amendment (1978) amended Art 359 so that the right to move the courts for Arts 20 and 21 can never be suspended. 2. All other rights can be suspended by Presidential order, so the answer is Articles 20 and 21.

examples.q: Which Article in the fundamental duty applies, when a construction worker takes his 8-year son to the site rather than sending him to school? Article 51A (h) / 51A (i) / 51A (j) / 51A (k) (CGL 2024)
examples.how: 1. Duty (k), added by the 86th Amendment (2002), requires a parent or guardian to give a child aged 6-14 opportunities for education. 2. An 8-year-old is in that range, so the answer is Article 51A(k).

examples.q: ______ Directive principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976. Three / Four / Five / Two (CGL 2024)
examples.how: 1. The 42nd Amendment added Art 39(f) on children, 39A on free legal aid, 43A on workers in management and 48A on the environment. 2. That makes four.

examples.q: Which of the following statements correctly applies the weighted voting mechanism under Article 279A(9)? (a) The Centre holds 75% of the voting power (b) A decision can be passed with the Centre and one State (c) The States collectively have twice the voting weight of the Centre (d) Each State has equal weightage as the Centre (CGL 2025)
examples.a: The States collectively have twice the voting weight of the Centre
examples.how: 1. The Centre holds one-third of the weighted votes and all States together hold two-thirds, so the States have twice the Centre's weight. 2. A decision needs three-fourths, so the Centre and one State cannot pass it. 3. Options (a) and (d) contradict the one-third and two-thirds split.

examples.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill. 2. Every Financial Bill is a Money Bill. Which of the above statements is/are correct? (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. A Money Bill (Art 110) contains only money matters, so it is a kind of Financial Bill, and statement 1 is true. 2. Financial Bills under Art 117 can contain other matters and are not Money Bills, so statement 2 is false.

examples.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 131 provides exclusive original jurisdiction to High Courts in federal disputes. 2. The Supreme Court can adjudicate disputes between States under Article 131. (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. Art 131 gives original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court, not the High Courts, so statement 1 is false. 2. Disputes between States, and between the Centre and States, are heard by the Supreme Court, so statement 2 is true.

examples.q: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council (ISC) is/are correct? A) The ISC is headed by the Prime Minister of India. B) It functions as a recommendatory body rather than a tribunal for dispute resolution. (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. The 1990 Presidential order under Art 263 makes the Prime Minister the chairman, so A is true. 2. The Council only inquires and recommends and cannot enforce or adjudicate, so B is true.

examples.q: Under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the period for default bail in minor offences (punishable with less than 10 years) is capped at: 30 days / 45 days / 60 days / 90 days (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. The BNSS keeps the old CrPC limits: 60 days for offences punishable with less than 10 years. 2. The 90-day limit applies to offences punishable with death, life or 10 years or more. 3. Once the limit passes, the Magistrate grants default bail.

examples.q: Match the subject matters with their Articles. 1. Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission; 2. Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections to legislatures; 3. Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters. A) Article 329, B) Article 324, C) Article 327. 1-C, 2-B, 3-A / 1-A, 2-C, 3-B / 1-A, 2-B, 3-C / 1-B, 2-C, 3-A (CGL Tier 2, 26 October 2023)
examples.how: 1. Art 324 creates the Election Commission and gives it superintendence, direction and control, so 1 goes with B. 2. Art 327 lets Parliament make laws on elections, so 2 goes with C. 3. Art 329 bars courts from interfering in electoral matters, so 3 goes with A. 4. The code is 1-B, 2-C, 3-A.

examples.q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India rule that, 'in case of any conflict between the fundamental rights and the directive principles, the former would prevail'? Champakam Dorairajan Case, 1951 / Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973 / Golak Nath Case, 1967 / Minerva Mills Case, 1980 (CGL Tier 2, 20 January 2025)
examples.how: 1. In State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) the Court struck down a caste-based admission order, holding that Directive Principles must conform to and run subsidiary to Fundamental Rights. 2. That judgment led to the First Amendment and Art 15(4). 3. Golak Nath and Kesavananda are about Parliament's power to amend, and Minerva Mills is about balance. 4. The answer is Champakam Dorairajan, 1951.

examples.q: Read the statements on the Doctrine of Repugnancy (Article 254). Statement I: If a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflicts with a Union law, the Union law prevails and the State law becomes void to the extent of the repugnancy. Statement II: A State law on a Concurrent subject that conflicts with a Union law can still prevail within that State if it has been reserved for and received the assent of the President. Which is/are correct? Only Statement II is correct / Both Statements I and II are correct / Only Statement I is correct / Neither Statement I nor II is correct (CGL Tier 2, 19 January 2026)
examples.a: Both Statements I and II are correct
examples.how: 1. Art 254(1) is the general rule that the Union law prevails and the State law is void to the extent of repugnancy, so Statement I is correct. 2. Art 254(2) is the exception: a State law reserved for the President and given assent prevails in that State, though Parliament can later override it, so Statement II is correct. 3. Both are correct.

examples.q: Which statements are correct regarding the Supreme Court judgment on the validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act? A. The Constitution Bench consisted of 5 judges. B. The Bench upheld the 10% EWS reservation by a 3-2 majority. C. As per the judgment, the 103rd Amendment is valid although it violates the Basic Structure. A, B and C / A and C only / B and C only / A and B only (CGL Tier 2, 7 March 2023)
examples.how: 1. Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (November 2022) was heard by five judges, so A is true. 2. The majority of three upheld EWS reservation against two dissents, so B is true. 3. The majority held that the amendment does not violate the basic structure; a law that violated it could not be valid, so C is false. 4. The answer is A and B only.

examples.q: Which of the following is NOT a qualification for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court? An advocate of a high court for at least ten years / A distinguished judge in the opinion of the President / A judge of a high court for at least five years / An advocate of the supreme court for at least ten years (CGL Tier 2, 20 January 2025)
examples.a: An advocate of the supreme court for at least ten years
examples.how: 1. Art 124(3) lists three routes: High Court judge for 5 years, High Court advocate for 10 years, or a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion (SSC's option says 'judge' for jurist). 2. There is no separate route for 10 years as a Supreme Court advocate. 3. So the option on a Supreme Court advocate is NOT a qualification.

revise: The key Parts are III for Fundamental Rights (12-35), IV for DPSP (36-51), IVA for Duties (51A), V for the Union, VI for the States, IX, IXA and IXB for local bodies and co-operatives, XI and XII for Centre-State relations, XV for elections, XVIII for emergencies and XX for amendment.

The Fundamental Rights groups are equality (14-18), freedom (19-22), exploitation (23-24), religion (25-28), minorities (29-30) and remedies (32, the heart and soul). Arts 20 and 21 are never suspended, and property is now under Art 300A.

DPSPs come from Ireland and are non-justiciable. Remember Art 40 for panchayats, 43 for cottage industries, 44 for UCC, 46 for SCs and STs, 48A for the environment and 50 for separating the judiciary; the 42nd added 39(f), 39A, 43A and 48A.

Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice, with the idea taken from the USSR. There are 11, the last, (k), added by the 86th in 2002, and paying tax, voting and respecting elders are not duties.

A presidential candidate must be 35, deposit Rs 15,000 and have 50 proposers and 50 seconders, and takes oath before the CJI. Impeachment is only for violation of the Constitution by two-thirds of total membership, while the VP is elected by MPs alone and sworn in by the President.

The Rajya Sabha has at most 250 members (245 now, 12 nominated, minimum age 30). The Lok Sabha has at most 550 (543 now, minimum age 25). Quorum is one-tenth, and joint sittings under Art 108 have happened three times.

A Money Bill starts only in the Lok Sabha, the Speaker certifies it, and the Rajya Sabha gets 14 days to recommend. Every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, and in a State it needs the Governor's recommendation.

For the Supreme Court remember 124(2) appointment, 131 original, 137 review, 139A transfer and 143 advisory. Judges retire at 65 and High Court judges at 62; the strength is being raised to 38 by the 2026 Bill, and Surya Kant is the CJI.

The Governor is appointed under Art 155, holds office under Art 156, takes oath before the High Court Chief Justice and pardons under Art 161 but cannot pardon a death sentence. A State ministry has 12 members to 15% of the Assembly, and Arts 165, 166 and 167 cover the Advocate General, business rules and the CM's duties.

Federal Articles: 246A gives GST power to both, 249 is the Rajya Sabha resolution, 250 is emergency legislation, 254 settles conflicts, 256 allows directions and 262 covers water. The Inter-State Council (263, 1990, PM, advisory) differs from the Zonal Councils (1956 Act, Home Minister).

Money Articles: 268 is stamp duty, 270 is shared taxes including GST, 280 is the Finance Commission (16th, Panagariya, 41%), 286 restricts taxes on inter-State trade and 293 covers State borrowing. The GST Council (279A) is chaired by the FM, weighted 1/3 to 2/3, and decides by 3/4.
Art 352 needs approval within 1 month by special majority, Art 356 within 2 months with a maximum of 3 years, and Art 360 within 2 months, when even judges' salaries can be cut.

Core amendments: 1st 1951, 7th 1956, 24th, 26th privy purses, 42nd mini-constitution, 44th property, 52nd anti-defection, 61st voting at 18, 73rd and 74th in 1992, 86th for 21A, 101st GST, 103rd EWS, 104th end of Anglo-Indian nomination and 106th women's reservation.
Case order: Anwar Ali Sarkar 1952, Berubari 1960, Golaknath 1967, Kesavananda 1973, Maneka 1978, Minerva 1980, Bommai 1994 and Puttaswamy 2017.

The new laws took effect on 1 July 2024: BNS replaced the IPC, BNSS replaced the CrPC (60/90-day default bail and video recording), and BSA replaced the Evidence Act (electronic evidence aligned with the IT Act 2000).

G|Sports.why: Sports gives about 2 questions per shift across 2021-2025 and is rising (1.9, 1.8, 2.0 and 2.2 in 2021-2024, then 2.4 in 2025). Rules and measurements, India's record at the Olympics, Asian, Commonwealth and World Cup events, and bodies, trophies and awards dominate. In 2025 about a third were two-statement or fill-in-the-blank items on exact rule details.

lines: The Olympics began at Olympia in 776 BC, and Pierre de Coubertin revived them with the IOC in 1894 and the Athens Games in 1896.
The five rings, first flown at Antwerp in 1920, stand for five continents, and 'Communiter' joined the motto in 2021.
Norman Pritchard's two silvers in 1900 opened India's account, and hockey's gold at Amsterdam in 1928 began a run of eight golds.
K.D. Jadhav won the first individual medal in 1952, Karnam Malleswari the first by a woman in 2000, and Abhinav Bindra the first individual gold in 2008.
Neeraj Chopra turned javelin into India's signature event, with gold at Tokyo 2020 and silver at Paris 2024.
India's best Olympics was Tokyo with 7 medals, while Paris 2024 gave 6, including Manu Bhaker's two bronzes.
Paralympians outshone everyone at Paris 2024 with 29 medals, a big jump from 19 at Tokyo.
India hosted the Asian Games in 1951 and 1982 and the Commonwealth Games once, in Delhi in 2010, and will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.
In cricket India holds two ODI World Cups, three T20 World Cups including 2026, the 2025 Champions Trophy and its first Women's World Cup in 2025.
A badminton court is 13.40 m long for everyone, and only its width grows from 5.18 m to 6.10 m for doubles.
Football's penalty mark sits 11 m from goal, a hockey umpire pointing to the centre means a goal, and cricket stumps stand 28 inches high.
On the track, lanes are 1.22 m wide, every hurdles race has 10 flights, and the relay baton changes hands in a 30 m zone.
Backstroke is the only swimming race that starts in the water, and a judo bout ends at once on ippon or hansoku-make.
In kabaddi a tie after 5 raids each goes to a fresh toss and a single Golden Raid, and a yellow card means 2 minutes off.
D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed chess World Champion in 2024, and India won both Olympiad golds that year.
The Khel Ratna, now named after Dhyan Chand, is celebrated alongside National Sports Day on his birthday, 29 August.

chapters.h: The Olympic movement: history, symbols and hosts
chapters.intro: The Olympics began in ancient Greece and were revived in modern form in 1896. SSC asks about the founder, the symbols, the firsts (flame, torch relay, women) and the host cities, so learn this chapter as one continuous story from Olympia to Brisbane.

items.what: The ancient Games were held at Olympia in Greece in honour of Zeus.
Pierre de Coubertin founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in Paris; its headquarters is now in Lausanne, Switzerland. {PYQ 2024}
The first modern Olympics opened in Athens on 6 April 1896. {PYQ 2023}
Women competed for the first time, at the Paris Games.
The Olympic flag with five rings was first flown, at Antwerp.
The first Winter Olympics were held at Chamonix, France.
The Olympic flame was lit for the first time, at Amsterdam.
The torch relay from Olympia began with the Berlin Games.
The first Paralympic Games were held in Rome. {PYQ 2023}
From Lillehammer onwards, the Summer and Winter Games have been held two years apart. {PYQ 2022}
The IOC added 'Communiter' (Together) to the Olympic motto.
Kirsty Coventry of Zimbabwe became IOC President, the first woman and the first African in the post.

blocks.title: The five rings
blocks.body: Picture the five rings as a family photo of the world: three on top (blue, yellow, black) and two below (green, red) on a white flag. By the traditional reading, blue is Europe, yellow Asia, black Africa, green Oceania and red the Americas. The motto Citius, Altius, Fortius means Faster, Higher, Stronger.

items: The Olympic flag carries 5 interlaced rings. {PYQ 2023}
Motto: Citius, Altius, Fortius (Faster, Higher, Stronger); Communiter (Together) added in 2021.

blocks.title: IOC and Games: extra facts
items: The IOC has 206 National Olympic Committees, and host cities are chosen by a secret ballot of IOC members.
Beijing is the first city to have hosted both the Summer (2008) and Winter (2022) Games.
South Africa has never hosted the Olympics.
An Olympic gold medal is mostly silver (at least 92.5 percent), plated with at least 6 grams of pure gold.
Thomas Hicks of the USA won the marathon at the 1904 Games, the first American man to do so.
In artistic gymnastics women compete on four apparatus (vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor), while men compete on six. {PYQ 2026}

chapters.h: India at the Summer Olympics: the medal story
chapters.intro: India's Olympic history is a favourite source of 'first Indian' and 'in which Games' questions. Read it as a timeline: each Games adds one new first, and SSC usually asks for that first.

items.what: Norman Pritchard, an Anglo-Indian athlete, won two silvers (200 m sprint and 200 m hurdles), India's first Olympic medals. {PYQ 2025}
India sent its first official Olympic team, and Purma Banerjee was India's first Olympic flag bearer.
India sent 8 athletes, and the first 'Indian Olympic Games' (national games) were held at Lahore the same year. {PYQ 2024}
Hockey made its Olympic debut and won India's first gold; Jaipal Singh Munda captained the team and Dhyan Chand starred from 1928 to 1936. {PYQ 2024}
K.D. Jadhav won wrestling bronze, India's first individual medal. {PYQ 2024}
India lost the hockey final 0-1 to Pakistan and took silver, the break in the gold run. {PYQ 2022}
P.T. Usha finished fourth in the 400 m hurdles, missing bronze by one-hundredth of a second. {PYQ 2025}
Leander Paes made his Olympic debut. {PYQ 2025}
Leander Paes won tennis bronze in his second Games, India's first Olympic tennis medal. {PYQ 2025}
Karnam Malleswari won weightlifting bronze, the first Olympic medal by an Indian woman; India won no boxing medal. {PYQ 2025}
Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won double-trap silver, India's first shooting medal. {PYQ 2025}
Abhinav Bindra won 10 m air rifle gold, India's first individual gold; Vijender Singh (boxing) and Sushil Kumar (wrestling) won bronze. {PYQ 2024, 2025}
Six medals, including India's first badminton medal (Saina Nehwal) and Mary Kom's boxing bronze.
Two medals: P.V. Sindhu won badminton silver and Sakshi Malik won bronze, the first Olympic medal by an Indian woman wrestler.

blocks.title: Why the ball is standardised

blocks.title: Dismissals and terms
items: The modes of dismissal are bowled, caught, LBW, run out, stumped, hit wicket, obstructing the field (which now includes handling the ball), timed out and hit the ball twice.

items: Strike rate is runs scored divided by balls faced, multiplied by 100: it shows runs per 100 balls.

The Test over rate is 15 overs an hour; an ODI innings is 50 overs.
A chinaman is a left-arm wrist-spin delivery that turns into a right-handed batter.
The first slip stands beside the wicketkeeper, on the off side behind the batter.
Cricket grounds are oval or circular.

blocks.body: A pawn that reaches the last rank can promote to a queen, rook, bishop or knight, never to a king or pawn, and promotion is not limited to pieces already captured. En passant lets a pawn capture an enemy pawn that has just moved two squares past it, but only on the very next move.

method: 1. Sort the question first: is it a rule or measurement, a term-to-sport match, an Indian first or record, a host and year, a body, trophy or award, or a recent event?

2. For a rule, check the number and the unit before anything else (m versus cm, every 2 points versus every point, 3 versus 5 seconds, white versus blue), because SSC changes one detail to make a statement false.
3. For history, place the event on the Olympic year line (1900, 1928, 1952, 1996, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024) and then match the sport.
4. For hosts, recall each sequence table (Olympics, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, World Cups) as one line, including the next two editions.

5. For current events, keep a monthly list of Indian winners and hosts from the last 18 months (league winners, national championships, World Cups, Khelo India, National Games) and revise it in the last week.
6. For two-statement items, mark each statement true or false separately before looking at the options.
7. Eliminate options that swap two real facts, such as the Durand and Santosh namesakes, Barcelona and Atlanta, or singles and doubles width.
traps: The badminton singles width is 5.18 m and the doubles width is 6.10 m, but the length of 13.40 m is the same for both.
In table tennis at 10-10, service alternates after every point, not every two points.
In judo the first-called player wears white, not blue, and hansoku-make is a disqualification, not a minor penalty.
In kabaddi a yellow card means 2 minutes off while green is only a warning, and a tie after 5-5 raids goes to a fresh toss and a Golden Raid.
In chess en passant is allowed only on the very next move, and promotion is not limited to pieces already captured.
Leander Paes debuted at Barcelona 1992 but won his medal at Atlanta 1996; Rathore's 2004 medal was silver, and Bindra's 2008 gold was the first individual gold.
India has hosted the ODI World Cup four times but never in 1983 (held in England); a 2022 key said 3 because it was set before 2023.
India did not win hockey gold in 1960 (it took silver) but did win gold in 1980.
The Durand Cup (1888, Shimla) is football and is named after Sir Mortimer Durand, while the Santosh Trophy is named after Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury.
S. Vijayalakshmi is the SSC-key answer for 'first Indian woman GM', although Koneru Humpy was the first to earn the full GM title, so read the options carefully.
Backstroke is the only stroke started in the water, and the 110 m hurdles has 10 flights, not 11.
The Commonwealth Games started in 1930 at Hamilton, Canada, not in England, and India has hosted only once (2010).
The relay exchange zone is 30 m under current rules, while older books give 20 m plus a 10 m acceleration zone.
At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics India won 19 medals and was 24th, while at Paris 2024 it won 29 and was 18th; do not mix them up.

examples.q: The length of the badminton court for singles is: 13.55 m / 13.40 m / 13.44 m / 14 m (CGL 2023)
examples.how: 1. A badminton court is 13.40 m long for both singles and doubles. 2. Only the width differs: 5.18 m singles, 6.10 m doubles.

examples.q: What should be the standard length of a tennis court according to the ITF (2021)? 23.77 m / 22.45 m / 26.42 m / 25.34 m (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. A tennis court is 78 ft = 23.77 m long. 2. Width: 8.23 m singles, 10.97 m doubles.

examples.q: The number of flights in a 110 m hurdle race is: 8 / 9 / 10 / 11 (CGL 2023)
examples.how: 1. The 110 m (men), 100 m (women) and 400 m hurdles all have 10 hurdles (flights). 2. Only the spacing and height differ.

examples.q: Which of the following strokes in swimming does NOT start with a dive into the pool from outside? Butterfly / Backstroke / Breaststroke / Freestyle (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. Backstroke swimmers start in the water, holding the starting grips and facing the wall. 2. The other three strokes start with a dive from the blocks.

examples.q: What is the distance of the penalty mark from the midpoint of the goal post in football? 10 m / 15 m / 11 m / 13 m (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. The penalty mark is 11 m (12 yards) from the midpoint of the goal line. 2. The penalty area extends 16.5 m; the centre circle radius is 9.15 m.

examples.q: In which of the following Olympic games did India NOT win Gold? 1948 / 1928 / 1932 / 1960 (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. India's hockey golds: 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980. 2. At Rome 1960 India lost the final 0-1 to Pakistan and took silver.

examples.q: India hosted the Asian Games in which of the following years? 1954 and 1982 / 1951 and 1986 / 1951 and 1982 / 1954 and 1986 (CGL 2024)
examples.how: 1. The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951. 2. New Delhi hosted again in 1982 (Asiad, which also brought colour TV to India).

examples.q: How many times has India hosted the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup (One Day)? 2 / 1 / 4 / 3 (CGL 2022)
examples.how: 1. Before the 2023 edition India had co-hosted 1987 (with Pakistan), 1996 (with Pakistan and Sri Lanka) and 2011 (with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh), so the key is 3. 2. After India hosted 2023 alone the count is 4; answer for the date of the question.

examples.q: Consider the following statements about judo: 1) The competition area has an inner contest area (minimum 8 m x 8 m) and an outer safety area (minimum 3 m wide). 2) The blue-uniform contestant is called first, followed by the white. Which is/are correct? (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. IJF rules: contest area at least 8 m x 8 m with a safety area at least 3 m, so 1 is true. 2. The first-called judoka wears white and the second blue, so 2 is false.

examples.q: Consider the following statements about service rules in table tennis: 1) At 10-10, service alternates every two points. 2) In the final doubles game, receiver order changes when one side reaches 5 points. Which is/are correct? (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. Normally service changes after every 2 points, but from 10-10 it changes after every point, so 1 is false. 2. In the last possible game of a doubles match the receiving pair changes order when one pair first reaches 5, so 2 is true.

examples.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Golden Raid and card system in Kabaddi? (a) Two Golden Raids are allowed before the result (b) A Green Card leads to a 2-minute suspension (c) A fresh toss is taken if the match is tied even after 5-5 raids (d) A Red Card results in a warning with no suspension (CGL 2025)
examples.a: A fresh toss is taken if the match is tied even after 5-5 raids.
examples.how: 1. In a tied knockout match each side gets 5 raids; if still level, a fresh toss decides who takes the single Golden Raid. 2. Green = warning, yellow = 2-minute suspension, red = suspension for the match, so (b) and (d) are false; (a) is false as there is one Golden Raid.

examples.q: Which of the following is true about 'en passant' in chess? (a) Only after the pawn moves two squares and waits a turn (b) Within two moves after the advance (c) Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares (d) Only if the capturing pawn is on a dark square (CGL 2025)
examples.a: Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares.
examples.how: 1. En passant lets a pawn capture an enemy pawn that has just advanced two squares past it, as if it had moved one. 2. The right exists only on the very next move; square colour is irrelevant.

examples.q: In which Olympic Games did Leander Paes make his debut before winning India's first Olympic tennis medal in the following edition? Barcelona / Atlanta / Sydney / New Delhi (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. Paes won bronze at Atlanta 1996. 2. The edition before that was Barcelona 1992, his debut. 3. Atlanta is the medal, not the debut; Sydney came later; New Delhi never hosted.

examples.q: Statements on India at Beijing 2008: 1) India won medals in shooting, boxing and wrestling, including its first-ever individual Olympic gold. 2) Saina Nehwal played women's singles badminton for India. Which are correct? (CGL 2025)
examples.how: 1. Beijing 2008 medals: Bindra gold (shooting, first individual gold), Vijender bronze (boxing), Sushil bronze (wrestling), so 1 is true. 2. Saina Nehwal played singles there and reached the quarter-finals (her medal came in 2012), so 2 is true.

examples.q: In a standard FIBA (international) basketball game, how many quarters are played, and how long is each quarter? Four 10-minute quarters / Four 12-minute quarters / Two 20-minute halves / Four 8-minute quarters (CGL Tier 2, 19 January 2026)
examples.how: 1. FIBA rules divide the game into four quarters of 10 minutes each, with overtime periods of 5 minutes. 2. The NBA in the USA uses four 12-minute quarters, which is the main distractor. 3. The answer is four 10-minute quarters.

examples.q: Statements on Aman Sehrawat at the Paris 2024 Olympics. Statement I: Aman Sehrawat won the bronze medal in the men's 57 kg freestyle wrestling event by defeating Darian Cruz. Statement II: With this win, at the age of 21 years and 24 days, he surpassed P.V. Sindhu to become India's youngest-ever individual Olympic medallist. Neither statement I nor II is correct / Only statement I is correct / Only statement II is correct / Both statements I and II are correct (CGL Tier 2, 19 January 2026)
examples.a: Both statements I and II are correct
examples.how: 1. Aman beat Darian Cruz of Puerto Rico 13-5 in the bronze bout of the 57 kg freestyle category, so Statement I is correct. 2. P.V. Sindhu had been the youngest Indian individual medallist (Rio 2016, aged 21 years and 1 month); Aman, at 21 years and 24 days, is younger, so Statement II is correct. 3. The answer is both.

examples.q: India hosted the 2025 Men's FIH Hockey Junior World Cup. Which option correctly states the location and timing? Bhubaneswar, Odisha, 15 to 30 November 2025 / Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, 1 to 15 December 2025 / Chennai and Madurai, Tamil Nadu, 28 November to 10 December 2025 / New Delhi, Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, 20 to 31 December 2025 (CGL Tier 2, 19 January 2026)
examples.a: Chennai and Madurai, Tamil Nadu, 28 November to 10 December 2025
examples.how: 1. The 2025 edition was moved to Tamil Nadu, with matches in Chennai and Madurai. 2. It ran from 28 November to 10 December 2025. 3. Bhubaneswar hosted the 2021 Junior World Cup and Lucknow the 2016 edition, which is why they appear as distractors. 4. The answer is the Chennai and Madurai option.

examples.q: In which sport did India defeat Pakistan 2-1 to lift the Men's Junior Asia Cup in 2023, overtaking them in the number of titles won at the event? Basketball / Hockey / Football / Badminton (CGL Tier 2, 20 January 2025)
examples.how: 1. The Men's Hockey Junior Asia Cup 2023 final at Salalah, Oman, ended India 2, Pakistan 1. 2. It was India's fourth title (2004, 2008, 2015, 2023), one more than Pakistan's three. 3. The answer is hockey.

examples.q: Match the positions in List I with the States in List II for the 36th National Games 2022. A. I position in medal tally, B. II position, C. III position, D. IV position with (i) Maharashtra, (ii) Haryana, (iii) Karnataka, (iv) Services Sports Control Board. A-i, B-iii, C-ii, D-iv / A-iv, B-i, C-ii, D-iii / A-i, B-ii, C-iii, D-iv / A-ii, B-i, C-iii, D-iv (CGL Tier 2, 26 October 2023)
examples.how: 1. National Games ranks go by gold medals. 2. Services topped the Gujarat games with 61 golds (A-iv). 3. Maharashtra was second (B-i), with the most total medals. 4. Haryana was third (C-ii) and Karnataka fourth (D-iii). 5. The code is A-iv, B-i, C-ii, D-iii.

revise: A badminton court is 13.40 m long, 5.18 m wide for singles and 6.10 m for doubles; a tennis court is 23.77 m long; a table tennis ball is 40 mm, lets are unlimited and service changes every point from 10-10.

The football penalty mark is 11 m from goal and the goal is 7.32 m x 2.44 m; cricket stumps are 28 inches, the ball 8.81-9 inches, the Test lunch 40 minutes, and a bowler gets 10 overs in an ODI and 4 in a T20.

Lanes are 1.22 m wide, the relay zone is 30 m, every hurdles race has 10 hurdles, the high jump runway is at least 15 m, backstroke starts in the water, and long jumpers take off from the stronger foot.
Kabaddi has 7 players, kho-kho 9 on the field, volleyball 6 and basketball 5; a black card in badminton is disqualification and a yellow card in kabaddi is 2 minutes off.
Jigoro Kano founded judo in 1882, it became Olympic in 1964, and white is called first; taekwondo means foot, fist and way; junior boxing rounds are 2 minutes with 1 minute of rest.
India's Olympic firsts run Pritchard 1900, hockey gold 1928 (8 golds, but silver in 1960), Jadhav 1952, Paes 1996, Malleswari 2000, Rathore 2004 and Bindra 2008.
Tokyo 2020 gave 7 medals with Neeraj's gold; Paris 2024 gave 6 (Neeraj silver, Manu's 2 bronzes, Swapnil, hockey and Aman); Paralympic medals rose from 19 to 29.

India hosted the Asian Games in 1951 and 1982; the next hosts are Aichi-Nagoya 2026, Doha 2030 and Riyadh 2034. The Commonwealth Games began at Hamilton in 1930, India hosted in 2010, Glasgow hosted 2026 and Ahmedabad hosts 2030.

India's cricket titles are the ODI World Cups of 1983 and 2011, the T20 World Cups of 2007, 2024 and 2026, the 2025 Champions Trophy and the 2025 Women's World Cup; India hosted the ODI World Cup in 1987, 1996, 2011 and 2023, and co-hosts 2031 with Bangladesh.

Spain won the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico (48 teams); the Durand Cup began at Shimla in 1888; the Santosh Trophy is named after Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury; the Subroto Cup is held in Delhi.

The IOC dates from 1894, the IOA from 1927 (Dorabji Tata), the IHF from 1925, the BCCI from 1928, the AAFI from 1946 and SAI from 1984; NSNIS was named on 23 January 1973, the PKL began in 2014 and the National Sports University is in Manipur.
The Khel Ratna was renamed after Dhyan Chand on 6 August 2021; the 2024 awardees were Manu Bhaker, Gukesh, Harmanpreet Singh and Praveen Kumar; National Sports Day is 29 August.
Anand was India's first GM and Barua the second; Gukesh became World Champion in 2024; Divya Deshmukh won the 2025 Women's World Cup; the bishop moves only diagonally.
The 36th National Games were in Gujarat, the 37th in Goa, the 38th in Uttarakhand (Services topped) and the 39th will be in Meghalaya in 2027; the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy goes to the best team.

Q|Percentage.why: Percentage has given about 0.9 direct questions per shift across 2021-2025, and about 0.6 per shift in 2025. It also drives Profit & Loss, Interest, Mixture and Data Interpretation, so its real weight is far higher. Successive change, savings, elections, population, price-consumption, 'more than' reversals and pass marks dominate.

lines: Per cent simply means 'out of every hundred', so x% is the fraction x/100.
Knowing that 1/8 is 12.5% and 1/6 is 16.67% lets you do in two seconds what decimals do in twenty.
Every percentage change is measured against the original value, which is the base.
The fastest way to handle any change is to turn it into a multiplier, so a 25% rise means multiply by 5/4 and a 20% fall means multiply by 4/5.
To undo a change, divide by the same multiplier instead of subtracting the percentage.
If A is 25% more than B, then B is only 20% less than A, because the base has changed.
Successive changes multiply rather than add, and for two changes the net result is a + b + ab/100.
A rise and then an equal fall of r% always leaves you r²/100 % poorer, whichever comes first.
When the price rises and spending stays fixed, consumption must fall by r/(100 + r) of itself, which is less than r%.
Income minus expenditure is savings, and the change in savings must be measured on the old savings, not on income.
Population and machine values grow or shrink year after year like compound interest.
An election flows from registered voters to votes cast to valid votes to candidates, and each percentage belongs to one stage of that flow.
In exams, the gap between two students' percentages equals the gap between their marks, including any 'fail by' and 'pass by' margins.
If a% of a number exceeds b% of it by k, the number is 100k/(a - b).
Before marking, check the base of the final percentage and whether the answer is an increase or a decrease.

chapters.intro: Per cent comes from 'per centum', which means 'in every hundred'. A percentage is just a way to compare any amount with 100, so that different amounts can be compared fairly. Scoring 18 out of 20 and 45 out of 50 look different, but both are 90 out of every 100, that is 90%. The whole topic rests on two small ideas: 'of' means multiply, and every percentage is taken of some base.

items: The sign % means 'out of 100'. So 25% means 25 out of 100, which is the fraction 25/100 = 1/4.
To turn a percentage into a fraction, divide by 100: 40% = 40/100 = 2/5.
To turn a fraction into a percentage, multiply by 100: 3/4 = 3/4 × 100 = 75%.
The word 'of' means multiply. 20% of 150 = 20/100 × 150 = 30.
100% of anything is the whole thing. 50% is half. 200% is double.
A percentage alone is not a quantity. '20%' means nothing until you ask '20% of what?' That 'what' is called the base.

blocks.title: Tiny examples to build the feel
rows: 10% is 6 and 5% is half of that, 3
rise of 20, measured on the old 80: 20/80
fall of 20, measured on the old 100: 20/100

items: Core idea 1, the base: a percentage change is always compared with the starting value. That is why ₹80 → ₹100 is a 25% rise but ₹100 → ₹80 is only a 20% fall. The gap is 20 both times, but the base differs.

Core idea 2, the multiplier: a rise of 20% turns 100 into 120, so it multiplies by 120/100 = 1.2 = 6/5. A fall of 20% multiplies by 80/100 = 0.8 = 4/5. Almost every question becomes a chain of such multipliers.
