blocks.title: Two cheating weights
blocks.body: When the buyer is also cheated, work with real kilograms. On 26 October 2023, B paid for 15 kg but received 15 × 0.95 = 14.25 kg, then sold it in 750 g "kilograms", that is 14.25/0.75 = 19 of them. Revenue 19 × 180 = 3420 against cost 2700 gives 26.67%. Multiplying 1000/750 alone gives 33.33%, a listed wrong option.

items.f: Three discounts: single equivalent = 1 - (1 - d₁)(1 - d₂)(1 - d₃)
Chain of n traders each at r%: first cost = final price/(1 + r)ⁿ
Buy n get m free: discount = m/(n + m)
Overall profit on separate deals = total profit/total cost

formulas.f: Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP
formulas.note: The basic definitions.

formulas.f: Profit % = (SP − CP)/CP × 100
formulas.note: Always on CP.

formulas.f: Loss % = (CP − SP)/CP × 100
formulas.note: Always on CP.
SP from CP for a profit p% or a loss l%.
CP from SP.

formulas.f: CP : SP = a : b ⇒ profit % = (b − a)/a × 100
formulas.note: The ratio form.

formulas.f: Profit as % of SP = p/(100 + p) × 100
formulas.note: A 25% profit on CP is a 20% profit on SP.

formulas.f: SP₂ − SP₁ = (p₂ − p₁)% of CP
formulas.note: Two selling prices; count a loss as a negative p.

formulas.f: Profit % at S₁ = loss % at S₂ ⇒ CP = (S₁ + S₂)/2
formulas.note: Equal gain and loss percentages.

formulas.f: Profit amount at S₁ = k × loss amount at S₂ ⇒ CP = (S₁ + kS₂)/(1 + k)
formulas.note: The gain is k times the loss.

formulas.f: CP of x items = SP of y items ⇒ profit % = (x − y)/y × 100
formulas.note: A negative result means a loss.

formulas.f: Gain = CP of g items on selling n ⇒ profit % = g/n × 100
formulas.note: If the gain equals the SP of g items, use g/(n − g) × 100.

formulas.f: Discount = MP − SP; Discount % = (MP − SP)/MP × 100
formulas.note: Always on MP.
SP after a discount of d%.
A discount of d% still leaves a profit of p%.

formulas.f: Net % = m − d − md/100
formulas.note: Markup m% followed by discount d%.

formulas.f: Required discount d = (m − p)/(100 + m) × 100
formulas.note: Markup m% and target profit p%.

formulas.f: Required markup m = (p + d)/(100 − d) × 100
formulas.note: Discount d% and target profit p%.

formulas.f: No profit no loss discount = m/(100 + m) × 100
formulas.note: After a markup of m%.

formulas.f: Successive discounts a, b ⇒ single = a + b − ab/100
formulas.note: For two successive increases use a + b + ab/100 instead.

formulas.f: Three discounts: 1 − (1 − a)(1 − b)(1 − c)
formulas.note: Multiply the remaining factors.

formulas.f: Single (a + b)% vs successive a%, b%: gap = ab/100 % of MP
formulas.note: For difference-of-discount questions with the same total.

formulas.f: Price raised x% then discount y% ⇒ real discount = y − x + xy/100
formulas.note: A negative result means a net rise.

formulas.f: Buy x get y free ⇒ discount = y/(x + y) × 100
formulas.note: Free-item offers.

formulas.f: n items for the price of m, sold at d% off ⇒ factor = (1 − d/100)(n/m)
formulas.note: A supplier bonus combined with a discount.

formulas.f: Sold at CP with weight w for 1000 ⇒ gain % = (1000 − w)/w × 100
formulas.note: False weight.

formulas.f: Profit p and weight x% less ⇒ factor = (1 + p/100)/(1 − x/100)
formulas.note: Use (1 − l/100) on top for a loss.

formulas.f: Weight used for gain g at CP = 1000/(1 + g/100)
formulas.note: Grams given per kilogram.

formulas.f: Equal SPs, x% gain and x% loss ⇒ loss % = x²/100
formulas.note: Always a loss.

formulas.f: Equal CPs, gains a% and b% ⇒ overall = (a + b)/2 %
formulas.note: Count a loss as negative.

formulas.f: Chain: final = CP × (1 ± p₁)(1 ± p₂)...
formulas.note: Dealers, wholesaler to retailer.

formulas.f: Festive re-mark: profit factor = k(1 − d)(1 + p)
formulas.note: Sold at P with profit p, then re-marked at kP with discount d.

formulas.f: Alligation on profit %: qty₁ : qty₂ = (p₂ − p̄) : (p̄ − p₁)
formulas.note: Parts sold at two profit rates.

formulas.f: Value ∝ weight²: loss fraction on cutting = 1 − Σaᵢ²/(Σaᵢ)²
formulas.note: Diamond or gem problems.

formulas.f: Partnership shares ∝ capital × time
formulas.note: After removing any charity or salary.
Fraction conversions used in almost every question.

method: 1. Read the last line first to see whether the answer is CP, MP, SP, a percentage or an amount, and whether it should be a profit or a loss.
2. If no amount is given, take CP = 100, or MP = 100 when only discounts are given; if an amount is given, keep the unknown as x.
3. Convert every step to a multiplier: +p% is (1 + p/100), −d% is (1 − d/100), a short weight is true/given, and n for the price of m is n/m.
4. Multiply the factors in the order of the story, then compare the product with 1 for a percentage, or equate it to the given amount.
5. When both MP and CP are unknown, use MP/CP = (100 + p)/(100 − d) or the net % formula instead of two equations.
6. For several items, find each CP separately, add them, and compute the percentage once on the total CP; never average percentages with different bases.
7. Use fraction equivalents such as 12.5% = 1/8 and 16⅔% = 1/6 so that numbers cancel, and approximate only at the end.
8. Before marking, check the base (profit on CP, discount on MP) and the sign (gain or loss) against the options.
traps: Taking profit % on SP or discount % on CP, when profit and markup are on CP and discount is on MP.
Adding successive discounts: 10% and 20% make 28%, not 30%, and two 15% discounts make 27.75%, not 30%.
Treating 'marked 30% above CP with a 17% profit' as a 13% discount, when it is 13/130 = 10% of MP.
Dividing by 1,000 instead of the weight actually given: 900 g for 1 kg is 100/900 = 11.11%, not 10%.
Using y/x instead of y/(x + y) for 'buy x, get y free': buy 5, get 2 free is 2/7, not 2/5.
Averaging percentages of different items: +20% and −10% on different CPs do not make +5% overall.
Calling equal SPs with x% gain and x% loss 'no profit, no loss', when the result is always a loss of x²/100 %.
In 'CP of 20 = SP of 18', dividing by 20 instead of 18, when the base is the number sold.
Forgetting overheads such as repair or transport in the CP before applying the profit percentage.
Giving SP when MP is asked, or the reverse, in 'discount d still leaves profit p' questions.
Picking a gain option when the result is a loss: a 20% markup with a 20% discount is a 4% loss.
In chains, applying the second dealer's percentage to the original CP instead of to his own buying price.
Reading 'buy 4, get 6' as 6 free, when it means 6 in all for the price of 4.
Rounding too early in ratio-of-SP questions, where options like 10.99% and 11.2% differ only in the decimals.

examples.q: (CGL 2022) A shopkeeper bought a cycle for ₹1,200 and sold it for ₹1,500. Find his profit or loss percentage.
(CGL 2024) Two successive discounts of 40% and 30% are equal to a single discount of:
examples.how: Step 1: Use a + b − ab/100 = 40 + 30 − 12 = 58%. Check: 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.42 of the price remains, so 58% is taken off.

examples.q: (CGL 2024) A shopkeeper marked the price 20% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 30%, find his loss percent.
examples.how: Step 1: Net % = 20 − 30 − (20 × 30)/100 = −16. Step 2: The negative sign means a 16% loss. Check: 1.2 × 0.7 = 0.84.

examples.q: (CGL 2022) By selling a car for ₹2,78,000, a dealer gains 25%. If the profit is reduced to 18%, the selling price will be:
(CGL 2023) If the cost price of 28 oranges is equal to the selling price of 24 oranges, then the profit percentage is:
examples.how: Step 1: Use (x − y)/y with x = 28 and y = 24. Step 2: 4/24 × 100 = 16⅔%. The base is 24, the number sold.

examples.q: (CGL 2024) After two successive discounts a toy with a marked price of ₹150 is sold at ₹105. If the first discount is 12.5%, what is the second discount?
examples.how: Step 1: After the first discount the price is 150 × 7/8 = 131.25. Step 2: 105/131.25 = 0.8 remains. Step 3: The second discount is 20%.

examples.q: (CGL 2022) In a certain shop the profit is 130% of the cost. If the cost increases by 28% and the selling price remains constant, what is the profit percentage to the nearest whole number?
examples.how: Step 1: Take cost 100, so SP = 230. Step 2: The new cost is 128, so profit = 102. Step 3: 102/128 × 100 = 79.7%, about 80%.

examples.q: (CGL 2022) A dishonest trader says he sells at cost price but uses a false weight and gains 12.5%. How many grams does he use for 1 kg?
examples.how: Step 1: Weight = 1,000/1.125 = 888.89 g. In fractions, a gain of 1/8 means he gives 8 parts for the price of 9, and 8/9 of 1,000 g is 888.9 g.

examples.q: (CGL 2022) A dishonest dealer sells a product at 11% loss on cost price, but uses 22% less weight. What is his percentage profit or loss?
examples.how: Step 1: The price factor is 0.89 and the weight factor is 0.78. Step 2: 0.89/0.78 = 1.141. Step 3: This is a gain of about 14.1%.

examples.q: (CGL 2022) Scheme I: two successive discounts of 15% and 25%. Scheme II: buy 5, get 3 free. Scheme III: buy 4, get 6. Which scheme is best for customers?
examples.how: Step 1: Scheme I is 15 + 25 − 3.75 = 36.25%. Step 2: Scheme II is 3/8 = 37.5%. Step 3: Scheme III means paying for 4 and taking 6, so 2/6 = 33.3%. Step 4: The largest discount is Scheme II.

examples.q: (CGL 2025) A retailer marks an air conditioner 80% above its cost price. He gives a discount of 25%, and then a further 10% on the discounted price. If the final selling price is ₹15,552, what is the cost price?

(CGL 2025) A mobile phone retailer sells a phone for P and earns a profit of 20%. For a festive offer he marks the same phone at 1.5P and gives a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage during the offer?
examples.how: Step 1: CP = P/1.2. Step 2: The offer SP is 1.5P × 0.9 = 1.35P. Step 3: The profit factor is 1.35 × 1.2 = 1.62, so the profit is 62%.

examples.q: (CGL 2025) A clothing store sold three dresses whose selling prices were in the ratio 5 : 6 : 7, with a profit of 20% on the first, a loss of 10% on the second and a profit of 30% on the third. What was the approximate overall profit or loss percentage?
examples.how: Step 1: Take SPs 5, 6 and 7. Step 2: CPs are 5/1.2 = 4.167, 6/0.9 = 6.667 and 7/1.3 = 5.385, a total of 16.218. Step 3: The total SP is 18, so the profit is 1.782/16.218 = 10.99%, matching the 10.98% option.

examples.q: (CGL 2023) A shopkeeper bought apples for ₹3,600. He sold one-fifth at a 10% loss, one-fourth of the remaining at a 5% loss, and two-thirds of the rest at a 15% profit. At what price should he sell the remaining apples to earn 27% overall?
examples.how: Step 1: One-fifth costs 720 and sells for 648. Step 2: Of the remaining 2,880, one-fourth costs 720 and sells for 684. Step 3: Of the remaining 2,160, two-thirds cost 1,440 and sell for 1,656, leaving a last part costing 720. Step 4: The target SP is 3,600 × 1.27 = 4,572. Step 5: The last part must fetch 4,572 − (648 + 684 + 1,656) = 1,584.

examples.q: A dishonest dealer marks up his goods by 50% and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. He also uses a faulty balance which reads 1 kg for 900 g. What is his net profit percentage, rounded to the nearest integer? (CGL Tier 2, 6 March 2023)
examples.how: Step 1: Markup and discount give 1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2 of cost per 1 kg charged. Step 2: He gives only 900 g, so the multiplier becomes 1.2 × 1000/900 = 1.333. Step 3: Profit = 33.33%, about 33%.

examples.q: B purchased 15 kg apples at ₹180 per kg from a wholesaler who uses a 950 g weight for 1 kg. B sold all the apples at ₹180 per kg but used a 750 g weight for 1 kg. Find B's percentage profit, correct to 2 decimal places. (CGL Tier 2, 26 October 2023)
examples.how: Step 1: B pays 15 × 180 = ₹2,700 and receives 14.25 kg. Step 2: He sells 14.25/0.75 = 19 of his "kilograms" for 19 × 180 = ₹3,420. Step 3: Profit = 720/2700 = 26.67%.

examples.q: Find the single equivalent discount for successive discounts of 12%, 18% and 25% on the marked price of a car. (CGL Tier 2, 3 March 2023)
examples.how: Step 1: Price paid = 0.88 × 0.82 × 0.75 = 0.5412 of the marked price. Step 2: Single discount = 1 - 0.5412 = 45.88%.

examples.q: A man sells a mobile phone for ₹680 at a loss. If he had sold it for ₹1,070, his gain would have been double the former loss. Find the cost price. (CGL Tier 2, 20 January 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: Loss L = C - 680 and gain 2L = 1070 - C. Step 2: So 1070 - C = 2C - 1360. Step 3: 3C = 2430 and C = ₹810.

examples.q: Products pass through the hands of three traders, each selling at a 30% profit on his cost. If the last trader sold them for ₹300, how much did the first trader pay? (CGL Tier 2, 3 March 2023)
examples.how: Step 1: Each sale multiplies the price by 1.3. Step 2: First cost = 300/1.3³ = 300/2.197. Step 3: = ₹136.55.

revise: Profit and markup are on CP and discount is on MP, so CP/MP = (100 − d)/(100 + p).
Markup m with discount d gives a net m − d − md/100, and the discount for a target p is (m − p)/(100 + m).
Successive discounts combine as a + b − ab/100; for three or more, multiply the factors.
A single (a + b)% discount beats a% then b% by ab/100 % of MP.
Buy x, get y free is a discount of y/(x + y), and n for the price of m is a factor of n/m.
For false weights, the factor is (1 ± p) divided by the fraction of weight given; 900 g at CP is 11.11%.
The weight used for a gain g at CP is 1000/(1 + g).
Equal SPs with ±x% give a loss of x²/100 %, while equal CPs let you average the percentages.
CP of x = SP of y gives a profit of (x − y)/y.
Equal gain % and loss % at S₁ and S₂ give CP = (S₁ + S₂)/2.
In chains, multiply all factors, and divide back for the first CP.
For several items, add the CPs and compute the percentage once; for mixtures, compare total CP with total SP.
Festive re-marking at kP with d% off after profit p gives a factor of k(1 − d)(1 + p).
facts: Base rule: profit, loss and markup percentages are on CP, while discount percentage is on MP.
Successive discounts: the order in which successive discounts are applied never changes the final price.
Successive discounts: for a fixed total such as 40%, the pair farther apart (30% and 10%) gives a bigger combined discount than an equal pair (20% and 20%).
Markup and discount: an equal markup and discount of x% always leave a loss of x²/100 %, so 20% and 20% give a 4% loss.
False weights: a trader selling at CP with 900 g per kilogram gains 11 1/9%, and one using 800 g gains 25%.
Profit on SP: a profit of 25% on CP equals a profit of 20% on SP, and 20% on CP equals 16⅔% on SP.
Free items: 'buy 4, get 6' means 6 items in all for the price of 4, while 'buy 4, get 6 free' means 10 items for the price of 4.

R|Blood Relations.why: Blood Relations averaged about 1.5 questions per shift across 2021-2025 and jumped to about 2.4 per shift in 2025. From 2022 to 2024 almost every question was a coded symbol chain (A + B means A is the mother of B). In 2025 short plain-English chains and pointing or 'said' puzzles dominated, while coded chains and 6-7 member family puzzles still appeared.

lines: Every family question is a ladder of generations: grandparents two rungs up, parents one up, you and your siblings level, children one down.
The question 'How is X related to Y?' always wants 'X is Y's ___', so answer from Y's side.
A relation word gives a gender only to its subject: 'A is the brother of B' makes A male and tells you nothing about B.
Your parent's sibling's child is your cousin, but your own sibling's child is your nephew or niece.
Paternal means through the father and maternal means through the mother, so the mother's brother is the maternal uncle (mama).
Brother-in-law has three routes: your spouse's brother, your sister's husband, and your spouse's sister's husband.
In SSC, 'father's wife' is always the mother and 'mother's husband' is always the father.
The 'only son' of your own parent is you if you are male, and the 'only daughter' is you if you are female.
Collapse a pointing phrase from its last words backwards, replacing each pair of words with one person.
In coded chains, read the expression in overlapping pairs and flip any reversed key where the second letter is the subject.
'A is the father of B but B is not the son of A' means B is the daughter, because a negative can fix a gender.
In 'which expression shows' questions, check the subject first, the object last, the generation gap, and the final gender.
In family puzzles, place the married couples first, then their children, and finally use the counting conditions.
When a gender is truly missing, choose a neutral word such as child or sibling, or 'cannot be determined'.
Draw the tree as you read, with generations on levels, a double line for couples and a gender mark on every person.

Is Y's -> write the answer as 'X is Y's ___'

chapters.intro: Every family is a ladder, and each relation word tells you how many rungs to move up or down. If you count rungs correctly, the right answer usually names itself: two rungs up is a grandparent and two down is a grandchild. Keep every generation on the same horizontal level when you draw.

chapters.h: In-law relations, the most tested vocabulary
chapters.intro: Marriage creates a second family, and SSC loves asking about it. The key idea is that an in-law is someone connected to you through a spouse, either your own or your sibling's or your child's. Learn the three routes to brother-in-law and sister-in-law, because options often hide one of them.

rows: Father or mother of your spouse
Spouse's brother, sister's husband (jija), or spouse's sister's husband (co-brother)
Spouse's sister, brother's wife (bhabhi), or spouse's brother's wife

items.b: Sister-in-law; SSC often words the answer as 'Husband's sister'
My husband (female speaker) or my sister's husband

chapters.h: Gender: what is fixed and what is not
chapters.intro: Gender decides the final answer word, so treat it with care. A relation word fixes the gender of its subject only, and a name alone is never proof of gender in SSC keys when 'cannot be determined' is an option. Use only relation words and pronouns such as he, she, his and her.

items.title: Male words
points: Father, son, brother, husband, uncle, nephew.
Grandfather, grandson, father-in-law, son-in-law, brother-in-law.

items.title: Female words
points: Mother, daughter, sister, wife, aunt, niece.
Grandmother, granddaughter, mother-in-law, daughter-in-law, sister-in-law.

items: 'A is the brother of B' fixes only A as male, but 'A is the husband of B' fixes both genders.
'A is the father of B but B is not the son of A' means B is the daughter.
'2 is the daughter of 3 but 3 is not the mother of 2' means 3 is the father.
If a gender stays unknown, prefer neutral answers such as child, sibling, parent or grandchild, and otherwise 'cannot be determined'.

items: Siblings share parents: if A is the brother of B and B is the daughter of C, then A is the son of C. {PYQ 2026}
The spouse of a parent is the other parent: if D is the wife of Z and Z is the father of Y, then D is the mother of Y.
Always answer from the second person's side, because 'How is X related to Y?' asks 'X is Y's ___'.

blocks.q: A family consisting of D, P, W, Y and M is travelling to meet one another. W is travelling with his daughters, D and P. M is travelling with his maternal grandmother, Y. D is the mother of M. How is Y related to P?
steps: W travels with his daughters D and P, so W is their father and D and P are sisters.
Y is M's maternal grandmother, i.e. the mother of M's mother.
D is M's mother, so Y is D's mother (and W's wife).
Siblings share parents, so Y is also the mother of P.
Answer: Mother.

steps: Note X and Y in the final question.
Draw each fact onto the tree through its shared name.
Walk from Y to X counting generation steps.
Name the relation using X's gender.

A is the son of B, B is the brother of C (C male)
items.b: C is A's paternal uncle; if C's gender is unknown the answer is uncle or aunt.

blocks.body: Use conditions such as 'a family of four with only one child' to merge people: the only child of one couple is the same person as the child mentioned elsewhere.

chapters.intro: Here a speaker describes someone through a long possessive phrase. The trick is to peel the phrase from the end backwards, replacing each two-word piece with one person, like folding a long rope. Always fix the speaker's gender first, because 'only son' and 'only daughter' often point back to the speaker.

blocks.title: Peeling a phrase
steps: Identify the speaker and his or her gender.
Start at the end nearest the speaker, for example 'my father's wife'.
Replace that piece with one person (my mother), then join the next word.
Repeat until one relation remains.

items.a: The only daughter of my mother's father
The only son of my grandfather

items: 'Her father is the only son of my father's wife', said by a man, makes her the speaker's daughter.
'This man's son's sister is my daughter', said by a woman, means the man's children are hers, so she is his wife.
'My father-in-law's son's only sister's mother-in-law' (male speaker) is my wife's mother-in-law, which is my mother. {PYQ 2026}

blocks.q: Rahul said, "The woman is the mother of the husband of the only daughter of my wife's mother." How is the woman related to Rahul?
steps: Peel the phrase from the end: start with 'my wife's mother', who is Rahul's mother-in-law.
Her only daughter is Rahul's wife.
The husband of Rahul's wife is Rahul himself.
The woman is the mother of Rahul.
Answer: Mother.
blocks.trick: 'Only daughter of my wife's mother' is always my wife, so 'her husband' collapses to the speaker.

chapters.intro: The words 'only son' and 'only daughter' usually point back to the speaker or the listener. Check that possibility before you invent a new person. These cases show the idea from different angles.

rows: Madhu (female): 'His mother is my mother's only daughter.'
The only daughter is Madhu herself, so Madhu is the boy's mother.
A man to a woman: 'His mother is the only daughter of your father.'
That daughter is the woman herself, so she is the mother of the man in the photograph.
'He is the son of my grandfather's only son.'
The grandfather's only son is the speaker's father, so the boy is the speaker's brother. {PYQ 2026}
'The daughter of the only child of my grandfather'
The only child is my father or mother, so she is my sister or me.

blocks.body: 'My mother's only son' said by a woman is her brother, not herself. The 'only son equals me' shortcut works only for a male speaker.

blocks.q: Pointing to a photograph, Amit said, "She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather." How is the person in the photograph related to Amit?
steps: Peel the phrase from the end nearest Amit: 'my grandfather' is Amit's grandfather.
The only son of Amit's grandfather is Amit's father.
The person is the daughter of Amit's father.
A daughter of your father is your sister.
Answer: Sister.
blocks.trick: 'Only son of my grandfather' always collapses to 'my father', so his daughter is the speaker's sister.

chapters.intro: Some phrases always collapse the same way, and knowing them saves a full drawing. Notice that many of them have two possible answers, one being the speaker. Choose between them using the gender and the options.

rows: Son of my father or mother
Daughter of my father or mother
Son of my grandfather or grandmother
Daughter of my grandfather or grandmother
Mother, when the father is their only son

chapters.intro: From 2022 to 2024 this was the dominant form. Each symbol stands for a relation, and an expression is read in overlapping pairs, like links in a chain. Before you start, rewrite the key in a mini table and flip any reversed definitions.

blocks.title: A typical key
rows: A is the mother of B
A is the brother of B
A is the wife of B
A is the father of B

blocks.title: Reading P x Q / R - S
steps: P x Q: P is the wife of Q.
Q / R: Q is the father of R.
R - S: R is the brother of S.
Combine: P is the mother of both R and S.

items: Reversed keys such as 'A @ B means B is the father of A' or 'A # B means B is the wife of A' make the second letter the subject; rewrite them before solving.
A half-relation key such as 'A ^ Z means A is the brother of Z's father' (paternal uncle) is treated as one step.
When options are compound, answer with a compound phrase such as 'Mother's mother', 'Father's sister' or 'Son's wife's father's mother'. {PYQ 2026}
Digits can replace letters, as in '4 + 3 / 2 / 1 - 5'; treat each digit as a person.

blocks.q:
In a certain code language,
A % B means 'A is the sister of B'
A € B means 'A is the son of B'
A = B means 'A is the father of B'
A ? B means 'A is the daughter of B'
Based on the above, how is B related to X if 'B % C ? O € P = X'?
steps: Rule: decode each symbol into a plain relation and read the chain one link at a time.
B % C: B is the sister of C (B is female). C ? O: C is the daughter of O. So B is also O's daughter.
O € P: O is the son of P (O is male). P = X: P is the father of X. So O and X are children of P; O is X's brother.
B is the daughter of O, who is X's brother.
Answer: Brother's daughter

blocks.cap: Decode one symbol at a time and place each person: O and X are P's children, and B is O's daughter, so B is X's brother's daughter.

blocks.q:
In a certain code language,
P # Q means 'P is the sister of Q'
P $ Q means 'P is the son of Q'
P @ Q means 'P is the father of Q'
P & Q means 'P is the daughter of Q'
Based on the above, how is Y related to M if 'Y # Z & N $ O @ M'?
steps: Rule: decode each symbol into words, then join the links one at a time.
Y # Z: Y is the sister of Z. Z & N: Z is the daughter of N. So Y is also a daughter of N.
N $ O: N is the son of O. O @ M: O is the father of M. So N and M are both children of O, and N (a son) is M's brother.
Y is the daughter of M's brother.
Answer: Brother's daughter

blocks.q:
In a certain code language,
A @ B means 'A is the mother of B',
A × B means 'A is the wife of B',
A + B means 'A is the brother of B' and
A ÷ B means 'A is the father of B'.
How is S related to H if 'S × D ÷ R + Y @ H'?
steps: Decode one symbol at a time: S × D means S is the wife of D.
D ÷ R means D is the father of R, so S and D are R's parents.
R + Y means R is the brother of Y, so Y is also a child of S and D.
Y @ H means Y is the mother of H.
S is the mother of Y, and Y is H's mother.
Answer: Mother's mother.

chapters.h: Type 4: Which expression shows a given relation
chapters.intro: Here the relation is fixed and you must find the expression that produces it, such as 'Which expression shows that P is the mother of R?'. You do not need to solve every option fully. Test each one only for subject, object, generation gap and final gender.

blocks.title: Fast elimination
steps: Reject options in which the required subject is not first or the object is not last.
Reject options whose middle links change the generation count.
Check that the gender of the final relation is fixed, for example that Q is followed by a male symbol when Q must be a son.
Confirm the survivor by reading it in pairs.

blocks.title: Patterns to recognise
rows: P is the mother of R
P mother of Q, and Q brother of R
P is the father of R
P father of Q, and Q sister of R
P brother of Q, and Q father of R
P mother of Q, and Q father of R (maternal needs Q to be R's mother)

chapters.h: Type 5: Family puzzles with many members
chapters.intro: These give six to eight members with conditions such as 'three generations', 'only two married couples' or 'S has only two children of the same gender'. They look heavy but follow a fixed order of work. Every fact must be used, and if two placements fit, the remaining statement decides.

blocks.title: Order of work
steps: Place the married couples first.
Hang the named children under them.
Attach spouses of children and then grandchildren.
Use the counting conditions to finish, keeping a gender list beside the tree.

items: Typical questions ask who is the mother or father of X, how many males or females there are, how X is related to Y, or which pair is a married couple.
A clause such as 'H has only two children, B and C' closes the family, so everyone else must be a spouse or a grandchild.
The mother of C's son is C's wife, and therefore H's daughter-in-law.
Three levels above and three below are enough for any exam question.

blocks.body: Do not count a married-in person as a blood member of the other branch of the family.

chapters.h: When the answer is 'cannot be determined'
chapters.intro: Sometimes the chain simply never tells you a gender, and the honest answer is a neutral word or 'cannot be determined'. Choose it only when a gender or a link is truly missing, not just because the chain is long.

rows: D is the brother of B; M is the brother of B; K is the father of M; T is the wife of K
B is T's son or daughter
M is the sister of K; D is the brother of K; F is the mother of M
K is F's son or daughter
K could be male or female.
K is the brother of T; M is the mother of K; W is the brother of M
The mother link decides that the side is maternal.

blocks.body: Bank-style sets offer 'data inadequate' as an option. Pick it only when a gender or link is genuinely missing.

chapters.h: Type 6: True-false statements and odd forms
chapters.intro: A few questions twist the usual format. The method stays the same: build the full tree once, then test each option against it.

rows: Which statement is correct or NOT correct (from a coded chain)
Build the full tree once, then test each option.
Which two symbols should be interchanged, or which sequence is right (2021)
Try each option on the given expression.
How many generations are there, or who is in the oldest one
The only child of my grandfather is my father or mother, so that person's daughter is my sister or me.

chapters.intro: The question style has swung between coded chains and plain-English puzzles. For 2026 all three families are live: plain chains, pointing puzzles and coded chains. Practise each until you can solve it in under 40 seconds.

items.what: About 0.9 per shift, with few coded chains and mostly long pointing puzzles plus a 7-9 member statement puzzle.
About 2 per shift, almost all coded, including 'Which expression shows that P is the ___ of R?'.
About 1 per shift, coded chains with 4-5 links, compound answers and some 'which statement is NOT correct' items.
About 2.4 per shift: roughly half plain 3-4 link chains, over a third pointing puzzles, plus a few coded chains and family puzzles.

chapters.intro: Across the 8 official Tier 2 Paper I papers with a Reasoning section (2, 3, 6 and 7 March 2023 for CGL 2022; 26 October 2023 for CGL 2023; 18 and 20 January 2025 for CGL 2024; 19 January 2026 for CGL 2025), 240 reasoning questions were asked, 30 per paper. Blood relations gave 15 of them, almost 2 per paper, plus one Venn-diagram item that the 2025 paper filed next to it. Tier 2 prefers coded chains. In March 2023 every paper had two questions built on the key # brother, @ daughter, & husband, % wife, and one chain (D @ N @ H & Y @ F % V) was reused in four questions. The January 2025 papers used the key + mother, - brother, x wife, / father and asked for four-step answers such as Wife's Father's Mother's Brother.

blocks.title: Blood relation questions in Tier 2 Paper I
rows: Coded chain with #, @, &, % (how is X related to Y)
Coded chain with +, -, x, / and a compound answer
Direct statements (U is the father of N ...)

blocks.title: Build the compound answer from the far end
blocks.body: For 'How is U related to Z?' start at Z and walk back to U one sign at a time. In U + V / W - Y x Z, the last sign Y x Z says Y is Z's wife, so the answer begins 'Wife's'. W - Y makes W her brother, so V, W's father, is her father: 'Wife's Father's'. U + V makes U his mother: 'Wife's Father's Mother'. The options differ in a single word (Father's or Mother's), so decide the gender at each step before you move on.

items: A parent of one sibling is the parent of the other, so if N is T's sister, N's father is also T's father.
A code fixes gender only for the person on the left of a gendered sign: A # B makes A male but says nothing about B.
In a husband-wife pair joined by & or %, a child of one is taken as the child of both, which is how SSC builds 'mother's mother' answers.
Tier 2 chains have five or six people. Draw generations on separate levels and write the gender mark as you read, and each question takes under a minute.
Reused chains are common within one exam cycle, so a chain you have solved once can be answered for any pair in seconds.

formulas.f: How is X related to Y? = X is Y's ___
formulas.note: Always answer from Y's side, because the reversed relation is the most common wrong option.

formulas.f: Parent's parent = grandparent; child's child = grandchild
formulas.note: These are two-level jumps.

formulas.f: Parent's brother = uncle; parent's sister = aunt; uncle's or aunt's child = cousin
formulas.note: Paternal is through the father and maternal is through the mother.

formulas.f: Sibling's son = nephew; sibling's daughter = niece
formulas.note: A spouse's sibling's child is also a nephew or niece.

formulas.f: Spouse's father/mother = father/mother-in-law
formulas.note: For a woman, her husband's mother is her mother-in-law.

formulas.f: Son's wife = daughter-in-law; daughter's husband = son-in-law
formulas.note: A parent's son-in-law is the speaker's own husband (female speaker) or her sister's husband.

formulas.f: Spouse's sibling, sibling's spouse, spouse's sibling's spouse = brother/sister-in-law
formulas.note: Three routes lead to the same word.

formulas.f: Father's wife = mother; mother's husband = father
formulas.note: This is the first substitution in most pointing puzzles.

formulas.f: Only son of my parent = me (male); only daughter of my parent = me (female)
formulas.note: This collapses the phrase back to the speaker.

formulas.f: Only daughter of my mother's father = my mother; only son of my paternal grandfather = my father
formulas.note: Each is a two-step collapse.

formulas.f: Only child of my grandfather = my father or mother
formulas.note: That person's child is therefore my sibling or me.

formulas.f: A op1 B op2 C = (A op1 B) and (B op2 C)
formulas.note: Read coded chains in overlapping pairs.

formulas.f: 'A @ B means B is ... of A' = reversed key
formulas.note: The second letter is the subject, so rewrite it before solving.

formulas.f: Male fixers: brother, father, son, husband, uncle, nephew; female fixers: sister, mother, daughter, wife, aunt, niece
formulas.note: The subject of each fact gets the gender, not the object.

formulas.f: 'A is father of B but B is not son of A' = B is daughter
formulas.note: Similarly, '3 is not the mother of 2' makes 3 the father.

formulas.f: Generation count: +1 per parent step, -1 per child step, 0 for sibling/spouse
formulas.note: Net +2 is the grandparent level; a parent step plus a child step gives a sibling or cousin level.

formulas.f: Mother's or father's only son's daughter = my daughter (male speaker)
formulas.note: This was a frequent 2025 pattern.

formulas.f: Grandmother of my father's only son (male speaker) = my grandmother; her daughter-in-law = my mother
formulas.note: This is a 2025 PYQ pattern.

formulas.f: Paternal uncle expression: P brother of Q, Q father of R
formulas.note: Used in which-expression questions.

formulas.f: Paternal grandmother expression: P mother of Q, Q father of R
formulas.note: For maternal grandmother, Q must be R's mother.

method: 1. Read the last line first: note X and Y in 'How is X related to Y?' and whether the options are single words or compound phrases.
2. In a coded question, rewrite the key in a mini table and flip any reversed definitions (B is the ... of A) before starting.
3. In a pointing question, identify the speaker and his or her gender, then collapse the phrase from the end, one relation at a time.
4. Draw the tree as you read, with generations on levels, = for couples and a gender mark on every person.
5. Walk from Y to X counting generation steps, then name the relation with X's gender.
6. If X's gender is not fixed, choose the neutral option (sibling, child) or 'cannot be determined'.
7. For 'which expression shows' questions, test the options only for subject, object, generation gap and final gender.
8. Recheck with one reverse reading: say 'Y is X's ___' and make sure it agrees.
traps: Answering Y's relation to X instead of X's relation to Y.
Fixing the gender of the object: 'A is the brother of B' says nothing about B.
Confusing cousin with nephew: a parent's sibling's child is a cousin, while your own sibling's child is a nephew or niece.
Confusing brother-in-law with father-in-law by skipping a generation when the chain contains a parent step.
Reading reversed key definitions (A @ B means B is the father of A) the normal way.
Treating 'my mother's only son', said by a woman, as herself; it is her brother.
Choosing 'Mother' when the chain gives 'Mother's mother' in compound options.
In 'which expression shows Q is the son of P' options, picking one where Q's gender is not fixed as male.
For 'the wife of my uncle's only son', answering cousin; the 2025 key gives sister-in-law (cousin's wife), so read the options for in-law forms.
Using names to guess gender when the options include 'cannot be determined'.
Reading 'father's wife' as a step-mother; SSC always intends the mother.
In family puzzles, counting a married-in person as a blood member of the other branch.

examples.q: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. How is A related to C? Options: Daughter, Son, Father, Uncle (CGL 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: B is C's daughter. Step 2: A is B's brother, so A is also C's child. Step 3: A is male, so A is C's son.

examples.q: A is the son of B. C is the wife of B. D is the son of C. How is A related to D? Options: Uncle, Brother, Cousin, Son (CGL 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: C is B's wife, so B and C are a couple. Step 2: A and D are both children of that couple. Step 3: A is male, so A is D's brother.

examples.q: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my father's wife.' Who is the woman to the man? Options: Sister, Cousin, Niece, Daughter (CGL 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: my father's wife is my mother. Step 2: her only son, for a male speaker, is me. Step 3: she is my daughter.

examples.q: A woman says, 'This man's son's sister is my daughter.' How is the woman related to the man? Options: Wife, Sister, Mother, Mother-in-law (CGL 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: the man's son's sister is the man's daughter. Step 2: she is also the woman's daughter. Step 3: the woman is the mother of the man's children, so she is his wife.

examples.q: Pointing to a woman, Raj said, 'She is the daughter-in-law of the grandmother of my father's only son.' How is the woman related to Raj? Options: Wife, Sister-in-law, Cousin, Mother (CGL 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: my father's only son is Raj himself. Step 2: Raj's grandmother's daughter-in-law is the wife of her son. Step 3: that is Raj's mother, as in the official key.

examples.q: Introducing Reshma to a guest, Karishma said, 'She is the daughter of my father-in-law's daughter.' How is Reshma related to Karishma? Options: Sister-in-law, Sister, Cousin, Niece (CGL 2021)
examples.how: Step 1: Karishma's father-in-law's daughter is her husband's sister, her sister-in-law. Step 2: that woman's daughter is Karishma's niece.

examples.q: Pointing towards the photograph of a lady, Varun said, 'She is my father-in-law's son's only sister's mother-in-law.' How is Varun related to that lady? Options: Brother, Son, Husband, Son-in-law (CGL 2021)
examples.how: Step 1: my father-in-law's son's only sister is Varun's wife. Step 2: her mother-in-law is Varun's mother. Step 3: so Varun is the lady's son.

examples.q: G is the brother of F. E is the father of K. C is the daughter of A. F is the mother of E. C is the sister of E. How is G related to A? Options: Brother's wife, Sister's husband, Husband's sister, Wife's brother (CGL 2024)
examples.how: Step 1: C and E are siblings. Step 2: C is A's daughter and F is E's mother, so A (the male parent) and F are the couple. Step 3: G is F's brother, so G is A's wife's brother.

examples.q: 'A + B' means A is the mother of B; 'A - B' means A is the brother of B; 'A x B' means A is the wife of B; 'A / B' means A is the father of B. If M + Q - R + K - Y, how is M related to Y? Options: Mother, Father's mother, Mother's mother, Brother's wife (CGL 2024)
examples.how: Step 1: M is Q's mother, and Q is R's brother, so M is also R's mother. Step 2: R is K's mother, and K is Y's brother, so R is Y's mother. Step 3: M is Y's mother's mother.

examples.q: A # B means A is the sister of B, A @ B means A is the son of B, A & B means A is the wife of B, A % B means A is the father of B. How is Q related to R if P & Q % L # R & K? Options: Sister, Mother, Father, Wife (CGL 2024)
examples.how: Step 1: P is Q's wife. Step 2: Q is L's father. Step 3: L is R's sister, so R is also Q's child, and Q is R's father.

examples.q: 'A ∞ B' means A is the sister of B, 'A * B' means A is the mother of B, 'A @ B' means B is the father of A, 'A # B' means B is the wife of A. If V ∞ U @ W # Y * Z, how is V related to Z? Options: Sister, Mother, Wife, Father (CGL 2022)
examples.how: Step 1: flip the reversed keys: U @ W means W is U's father, and W # Y means Y is W's wife. Step 2: Y * Z means Y is Z's mother, so U and Z are both children of W and Y. Step 3: V is U's sister, hence Z's sister.

examples.q: If A / B means A is the father of B, A - B means A is the mother of B, A + B means A is the brother of B, which expression shows that P is the mother of R? Options: Q - P + R, P - Q + R, P - Q / R, R + P - Q (CGL 2022)
examples.how: Step 1: in P - Q + R, P is Q's mother and Q is R's brother. Step 2: so R is also P's child, and P is R's mother. Step 3: the other options put P or R in the wrong place or give a grandmother.

examples.q: 'A ? B' means A is the mother of B, 'A ! B' means A is the wife of B, 'A & B' means A is the brother of B, 'A x B' means A is the father of B. Which means that Z is the wife's father's mother of L? Options: Z ? B x T & J ! L, Z ? B ! T & J x L, Z ! B x T ? J & L, Z & B ! T x J ? L (CGL 2024)
examples.a: Z ? B x T & J ! L
examples.how: Step 1: J ! L means J is L's wife. Step 2: T & J means T is J's brother, so they share a father. Step 3: B x T makes B that father, and Z ? B makes Z his mother. So Z is L's wife's father's mother.

examples.q: Six members 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 live together. 2 is the daughter of 3, but 3 is not the mother of 2. 1 and 3 are a married couple. 5 is the sister of 3. 4 is the daughter of 1. 6 is the brother of 2. Who is the mother of 2? Options: 2, 1, 4, 5 (CGL 2024)
examples.how: Step 1: 3 is 2's parent but not the mother, so 3 is the father. Step 2: 1 is married to 3, so 1 is the mother of 2.

examples.q: 'A # B' means A is the brother of B, 'A @ B' means A is the daughter of B, 'A & B' means A is the husband of B and 'A % B' means A is the wife of B. If D @ N @ H & Y @ F % V, how is N related to F? Options: Son's wife, Daughter, Daughter's daughter, Sister's daughter (CGL Tier 2, 2 Mar 2023)
examples.how: Step 1: N @ H makes N the daughter of H, and H & Y makes H the husband of Y, so Y is N's mother. Step 2: Y @ F makes Y the daughter of F. Step 3: so N is the daughter of F's daughter.

examples.q: Using the same key, if W % D # G @ B & M @ I, how is D related to M? Options: Father's father, Father, Grandson, Son (CGL Tier 2, 2 Mar 2023)
examples.how: Step 1: W % D makes D a man (W is his wife). Step 2: D # G makes D the brother of G, and G @ B makes G the daughter of B. Step 3: B & M makes B the husband of M, so G, and hence D, is M's child. D is male, so D is M's son.

examples.q: A + B means A is the mother of B, A - B means A is the brother of B, A x B means A is the wife of B and A / B means A is the father of B. How is U related to Z if U + V / W - Y x Z? Options: Wife's Mother's Sister, Wife's Father's Mother, Wife's Mother's Mother, Wife's Father's Sister (CGL Tier 2, 18 Jan 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: Y x Z makes Y the wife of Z. Step 2: W - Y makes W her brother, and V / W makes V the father of W and so of Y. Step 3: U + V makes U the mother of V. Reading from Z: wife, her father, his mother.

examples.q: With the same key, how is U related to Z if U - V x W / Y + Z? Options: Mother's father's father, Mother's father's brother, Mother's mother's brother, Mother's mother's father (CGL Tier 2, 20 Jan 2025)
examples.how: Step 1: Y + Z makes Y the mother of Z. Step 2: W / Y makes W the father of Y, and V x W makes V the wife of W, so V is Y's mother. Step 3: U - V makes U the brother of V. Reading from Z: mother, her mother, her brother.

examples.q: Pointing to Sakshi, a man said, 'She is the daughter of the brother of the son of my wife.' How is the man related to Sakshi? Options: Granddaughter, Grandson, Grandmother, Grandfather (CGL Tier 2, 19 Jan 2026)
examples.how: Step 1: the son of my wife is my son. Step 2: the brother of my son is also my son. Step 3: Sakshi is that son's daughter, so she is the speaker's granddaughter and the speaker, a man, is her grandfather.

revise: Answer in the form 'X is Y's ___', never the reverse.
Only the subject of a relation word gets a gender.
Father's wife is the mother, the only son of my parents (male speaker) is me, and the only daughter of my mother's father is my mother.
Collapse pointing phrases from the end, one pair at a time.
Read coded chains in overlapping pairs, and flip reversed definitions first.
A parent's sibling's child is a cousin, and a sibling's child is a nephew or niece.
Brother-in-law has three routes: spouse's brother, sister's husband, and spouse's sister's husband.
A parent's son-in-law, said by a woman, is her husband.
'Not the son' means daughter, and 'not the mother' means father.
In which-expression questions, check the subject first, the object last, the generation gap and the final gender.
In family puzzles, place couples first, then children, then use counting conditions.
When a gender is unknown, pick sibling or child, or 'cannot be determined'.
The 2025 papers mixed plain chains and pointing puzzles, while 2022-2024 were mostly coded, so practise both.

learn.h: Pointing and conversation questions: solve from the end
points: Rewrite the speaker's phrase from the last word backwards, and replace each piece with one person.
"His mother is my mother's only daughter", said by Madhu (female): the only daughter of Madhu's mother is Madhu herself, so Madhu is the boy's mother.
A man tells a woman, "His mother is the only daughter of your father": that daughter is the woman herself, so she is the mother of the man in the photograph.
"He is the son of my grandfather's only son": the grandfather's only son is the speaker's father, so the boy is the speaker's brother.
"Only son" or "only daughter" usually points back to the speaker or the listener. Check that before you look for a new person.
Son of father or mother = brother or oneself. Daughter of father or mother = sister or oneself.
Son of grandfather or grandmother = father or uncle. Their daughter = mother or aunt.
Mother of one's son = oneself or wife. Father of one's daughter = oneself or husband.
Only daughter-in-law of one's grandparents = mother (when the father is their only son).
Son's or daughter's grandson = great-grandson. Father's or mother's grandfather = great-grandfather.

learn.h: When the answer should be 'cannot be determined'
points: D is the brother of B; M is the brother of B; K is the father of M; T is the wife of K. B's gender is never given, so B is T's 'son or daughter'.
M is the sister of K; D is the brother of K; F is the mother of M. K could be male or female, so the answer is again 'son or daughter'.
K is the brother of T; M is the mother of K; W is the brother of M. W is on the mother's side, so he is T's maternal uncle. The mother link decides maternal or paternal.
Bank-style sets offer 'data inadequate' as an option. Pick it only when a gender or a link is truly missing, not when the chain is just long.
Clauses like 'H has only two children, B and C' close the family: no one else can be H's child, so everyone else must be a spouse or a grandchild.
Place the named children first, then attach spouses (the mother of C's son is C's wife, and so H's daughter-in-law), then the grandchildren.
Keep a generation count: three levels above and three below are enough for any exam question.

R|Series.why: Series is the biggest Reasoning head, with 5.16 questions per shift across 2021-2025 (5.08 in 2025). Letter-cluster and number series (next, missing or wrong term) appear in every shift, figure series were heavy in 2022-2024, and blank-filling letter patterns ran at about one per shift in 2023-2024. In 2025 wrong-term items became frequent, so prepare every format together.

lines: A series is a row of terms built by one fixed rule, and your only job is to find that rule and extend it or repair it.
The rule must fit every printed term, because a rule that fits only the first three terms is the most common way to lose this mark.
For letters, think in numbers: EJOTY gives E5, J10, O15, T20 and Y25, and every other letter can be counted from its nearest anchor.
Opposite letters always add up to 27, so A pairs with Z, B with Y and M with N.
The alphabet is a circle: go past Z by subtracting 26, and go before A by adding 26.
Number series are checked in a fixed order: differences, second differences, ratios, special numbers, alternate places and finally digit rules.
When numbers grow slowly, look at the gaps; when they roughly double or triple, try multiply-then-add; when they explode, suspect a growing multiplier.
SSC's favourite fast-growing series uses a changing multiplier such as ×1 + 2, ×2 + 2, ×3 + 2, so 37 becomes 39, then 80, then 242.
Terms that rise and fall are usually two series woven together or two operations taking turns.
Squares, cubes, n² ± 1, n(n + 1), n³ ± n, 2ⁿ ± 1, factorials and primes should be recognised on sight, not calculated.
In a letter cluster, every position is its own little series, so solve the first letters, strike options, then move to the second letters.
Mixed-case clusters carry two rules at once, the letter steps and the capital-small pattern, and both must match.
A blank-filling letter pattern is one block repeated, so find the block, write the whole line and read the blanks in order.
One wrong term spoils two neighbouring gaps, and the culprit sits exactly between those two broken gaps.
After repairing a wrong term, continue from the corrected value, and the next printed term will confirm your fix.
Figure series are solved one element at a time: rotation, position, count and shading, each tracked separately.

mnemonics.for: Letter positions in steps of five, the anchors for every letter series.
Letters whose positions are multiples of 3, handy for +3 series.

mnemonics.key: Do Smart Readers Skip Any Detail?
expand: D -> Digit rules, last of all
mnemonics.for: The order in which to test a number series.
